questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The team has developed a cutting-edge software for data analysis.

options.text: A cutting-edge software for data analysis is developed by the team.
A cutting-edge software for data analysis was developed by the team.
A cutting-edge software for data analysis has been developed by the team.
A cutting-edge software for data analysis had been developed by the team.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A cutting-edge software for data analysis has been developed by the team.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The active voice sentence follows the structure of the **Present Perfect Tense**: **Subject + has/have + V3 (Past Participle) + Object**. Here, **The team** is the subject, **has developed** is the verb, and **a cutting-edge software for data analysis** is the object.

• To transform a **Present Perfect** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the standard grammatical formula is: **New Subject (Object) + has/have + been + V3 + by + New Object (Subject)**.

• In the passive construction, the object **a cutting-edge software for data analysis** becomes the new subject. Since this subject is **singular**, it is paired with the auxiliary verb **has**.

• The word **been** is mandatory in perfect tense passive conversions to indicate the completed state of the action relative to the subject.

• The original subject **The team** is shifted to the end of the sentence as the **agent**, preceded by the preposition **by**.

• Combining these elements results in: **A cutting-edge software for data analysis has been developed by the team.**

 **Additional Information__**

• Voice Conversion Rules based on Tense:

• **Simple Present**: The passive form uses **is/am/are + V3**. (e.g., **is developed**). This is used for habitual actions or general truths.

• **Simple Past**: The passive form uses **was/were + V3**. (e.g., **was developed**). This indicates an action completed at a specific time in the past.

• **Past Perfect**: The passive form uses **had + been + V3**. (e.g., **had been developed**). This is used for an action completed before another point in the past.

• **Future Perfect**: The passive form uses **will have + been + V3**. This indicates an action that will be completed by a certain future time.

• Conceptual Importance:

• **Active Voice**: Used when the **doer** (The team) is the primary focus of the sentence.

• **Passive Voice**: Used when the **action** or the **result** (The software) is more significant than who performed it, or when the performer is unknown.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
By next month, the farmers will have harvested the crops.

options.text: The crops will have been harvested by the farmers by next month.
The crops are been harvested by the farmers by next month.
The crops will be harvested by the farmers next month.
The crops will being harvested by the farmers by next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The crops will have been harvested by the farmers by next month.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence **'By next month, the farmers will have harvested the crops'** is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Future Perfect Tense** structure (Subject + will have + V3 + Object).

• When converting to **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence, **'the crops'**, becomes the new subject of the passive sentence.

• The **Future Perfect** verb form **'will have harvested'** must be changed to its passive equivalent, which is **'will have been harvested'** (will have + been + V3).

• The original subject, **'the farmers'**, is introduced as the agent using the preposition **'by'**, resulting in **'by the farmers'**.

• The time indicator **'By next month'** remains consistent in the sentence to denote that the action will be completed by a specific future point.

• Therefore, the resulting sentence maintains the exact meaning and tense of the original while shifting focus to the entity being acted upon (the crops).

 **Additional Information__**

• **Future Perfect Passive Construction**:

• The general formula for **Future Perfect Passive** is: **Subject (Receiver) + will + have + been + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent (Doer)**.

• It is used specifically for actions that will have been completed before another point in the future.

• The addition of **'been'** is the critical identifier for the **passive transformation** in perfect tenses.

• **Comparison with other Tense Forms**:

• **Future Simple Passive**: Uses **'will be + V3'** (e.g., 'The crops will be harvested'). This indicates a general future action rather than a completed one.

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Uses **'has/have been + V3'** (e.g., 'The crops have been harvested'), which refers to a completed action in the past with current relevance.

• **Future Continuous**: Generally does not have a commonly used passive form in standard English (avoiding **'will be being'**).

</ul

questions.question:

The Prime Minister of Malaysia is appearing _______ television today at 8:30 p.m.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**on**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The **preposition** '**on**' is used when referring to **electronic media** and **broadcasting** platforms such as **television**, radio, or the internet. 
• The phrase '**appearing on television**' is a standard expression used to describe someone being shown during a broadcast. 
• The sentence indicates a scheduled broadcast featuring the **Prime Minister** at **8:30 p.m.**, making '**on**' the grammatically correct choice. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. **Complete Sentence:** *'The **Prime Minister** of **Malaysia** is appearing **on**__ television today at **8:30 p.m.**'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 2: 'in'** is generally used for **print media** such as **newspapers**, magazines, or **books** (e.g., 'in the newspaper'). 
• **Option 3: 'to'** is used to indicate **direction**, **motion**, or the **recipient** of an action. 
• **Option 4: 'with'** is used to indicate **accompaniment** or the **instrument** used to perform an action. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."
Many small investors got burns on their fingers in the stock market crash of 2008.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**got their fingers burnt**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence requires the correct usage of the **English idiom** 'to burn one's fingers' or 'to get one's fingers burnt'. This expression means to suffer **financial loss** or unpleasant consequences as a result of meddling in something or taking a risk.

• The context of the sentence is the **stock market crash of 2008**, which is a specific historical event in the past. Therefore, the verb must be in the **simple past tense** (got).

• The grammatical structure for this **causative expression** is **subject + got + object (their fingers) + past participle (burnt)**. The original phrase 'got burns on their fingers' is a literal and incorrect phrasing of the intended figurative meaning.

• In this context, **burnt** acts as the past participle modifying the state of the object (fingers) after the action of the **market crash**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Grammatical Analysis of Incorrect Options**:

• **Verb Tense**: The option **get their fingers burnt** is grammatically correct in structure but uses the **present tense**. This is incompatible with the year **2008**, which necessitates a past tense marker.

• **Idiomatic Precision**: The phrase **got burning fingers** is not a recognized idiom and implies a physical sensation rather than the metaphorical **economic loss** associated with the crash.

• **Contextual Background**:

• The **2008 Financial Crisis** was characterized by a massive devaluation of **securities** and **equities**, causing widespread losses for **retail investors** (small investors).

• The idiom **get one's fingers burnt** is standard in **financial journalism** to describe the risks of **speculative trading** or **market volatility**.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
"Yes my dear your sister's latest novel set in Venice has received rave reviews," said her mother.

options.text: Yes, my dear your sisters' late novel
Yes my dear, your sister's last novel
Yes, my dear, your sister's latest novel

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yes, my dear, your sister's latest novel**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires proper punctuation for an **interjection** and a **vocative expression**. The word **Yes** is an introductory interjection and must be followed by a **comma** to separate it from the main clause. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The phrase **my dear** is a term of **direct address** (vocative case). According to standard English grammar rules, a person or group being addressed directly must be set off from the rest of the sentence using **commas**. Since it follows an interjection, it needs a comma both before and after it. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The use of **sister's** is the correct **singular possessive** form, indicating that the novel belongs to one sister. The apostrophe is placed before the 's' to show ownership by a single entity. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• The term **latest** is the **superlative adjective** used to denote the most recent occurrence in a series. In the context of a **novel**, it implies the most recently published work, which fits the intended meaning of the sentence. Hence, statement 3 is correct.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Word Usage and Nuance**:
 
 
• **Latest vs. Last**: While **last** can mean the most recent, it often implies the final item in a sequence where no more will follow. **Latest** specifically highlights the most current work in an ongoing career.
 
• **Late**: Using **late** would imply the sister is deceased or that the novel was overdue, which changes the **semantic meaning** of the original sentence.
 
• **Sisters'**: This is the **plural possessive** form. It would only be used if the novel was co-written by multiple sisters, which is not suggested by the singular context of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation Importance**:
 
 
• Omitting the **comma** after **Yes** or around the **vocative** phrase **my dear** leads to a **run-on** effect that obscures the structure of **direct speech** in **narrative writing**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Identify the error.
"She insisted me to participate in the competition."
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the segment **me to participate**.
 
• The verb **insist** cannot be followed by an **object + to-infinitive** structure (e.g., insist someone to do something).
 
• Instead, **insist** typically takes the preposition **on** followed by a **gerund** (verb + ing) or a **that-clause**.
 
• The sentence should be corrected to: *'She insisted **on my participating** in the competition'* or *'She insisted **that I participate** in the competition.'*
 
• Therefore, the grammatical error is located in **part 2**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **me to participate**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'She insisted **on my participating** in the competition.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Insist on:** When we use **insist** with a noun or a gerund, we must use the preposition **on**. Example: *'He insisted **on** a receipt.'*
 
• **Insist that:** When using a clause, **that** is used. Example: *'He insisted **that** he was innocent.'*
 
• **In the competition:** This part is grammatically correct as it correctly identifies the event she is referring to.
</ul

• The error in the sentence lies in the use of the plural verb **are** (written as **äre** in the options) after the pronoun **Neither**.
 
• The word **Neither** is a **distributive pronoun** which is used to refer to 'not one and not the other' of two things or people.
 
• Grammatically, distributive pronouns like **Each**, **Either**, and **Neither** are always treated as **singular subjects**.
 
• According to the rules of **Subject-Verb Agreement**, a singular subject must be accompanied by a **singular verb**.
 
• Therefore, the plural verb **are** must be replaced with the singular verb **is** to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **äre**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'Neither of the solutions **is** correct.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neither of**: This phrase is followed by a **plural noun** or **plural pronoun** (solutions), but the **verb** remains singular because the focus is on each individual item not being correct.
 
• **Neither...nor**: In a correlative conjunction structure, if two subjects are joined by **nor**, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. However, when **neither** is used alone as the subject, it is strictly singular.
 
• Other examples: '**Neither** of the candidates **has** arrived yet' (Not 'have').

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. Mr. Rao woke up early every day to prepare his lessons. 

P. He taught his students with patience and kindness. 

Q. He spent extra time helping students after school. 

R. He encouraged slow learners and motivated them to improve. 

S. His students respected him because he cared for them. 

6. Mr. Rao felt happy seeing his students succeed in life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes the daily routine and professional dedication of a teacher named **Mr. Rao** and the resulting impact on his students.
 
• **Sentence 1** introduces the subject and his preparation: **'Mr. Rao woke up early every day to prepare his lessons.'**
 
• **Sentence P** logically follows by describing what he does with those prepared lessons: **'He taught his students with patience and kindness.'**
 
• **Sentence R** provides a specific detail about his teaching methodology: **'He encouraged slow learners and motivated them to improve.'**
 
• **Sentence Q** adds another dimension to his hard work, mentioning what he did after classes: **'He spent extra time helping students after school.'**
 
• **Sentence S** presents the outcome of his dedication: **'His students respected him because he cared for them.'**
 
• **Sentence 6** concludes the sequence with the final result of his efforts: **'Mr. Rao felt happy seeing his students succeed in life.'**
 
• The correct sequence is **PRQS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'**Mr. Rao** woke up early every day to prepare his lessons. He **taught** his students with **patience** and **kindness**. He **encouraged slow learners** and **motivated** them to improve. He spent **extra time** helping students **after school**. His students **respected** him because he cared for them. Mr. Rao felt happy seeing his students **succeed** in life.'</div

questions.question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts - P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

1. Mother's Day is a special day to honor and thank all mothers. 

P. It is celebrated every year to show love and appreciation. 

Q. Children give cards, flowers, and gifts to their mothers. 

R. Families spend time together and make mothers feel happy. 

S. Schools and communities conduct small programs to celebrate mothers. 

6. Mother's Day reminds us to respect and care for our mothers every day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins with **Sentence 1**, which introduces **Mother's Day** and its primary purpose: to honor and thank all mothers. 
• **Sentence P is the second sentence** as it explains the frequency and the broader intent behind the day: 
• 'It is celebrated every year to show love and appreciation.' 
• **Sentence Q follows** by providing specific examples of how individuals (children) express their love: 
• 'Children give cards, flowers, and gifts to their mothers.' 
• **Sentence R is the fourth sentence** as it transitions from physical gifts to the social and emotional aspect of family bonding: 
• 'Families spend time together and make mothers feel happy.' 
• **Sentence S is the fifth sentence** because it expands the scope of the celebration to institutional and community settings: 
• 'Schools and communities conduct small programs to celebrate mothers.' 
• The paragraph concludes with **Sentence 6**, which provides a lasting takeaway about the ongoing responsibility to care for mothers. 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

'**Mother's Day** is a special day to honor and thank all mothers. It is celebrated every year to show **love and appreciation**. Children give **cards, flowers, and gifts** to their mothers. Families spend **time together** and make mothers feel happy. Schools and communities conduct **small programs** to celebrate mothers. **Mother's Day** reminds us to **respect and care** for our mothers every day.'</div
